summary: Latency regression (p95 decode) on Dedicated after enabling quantization profile on one route
description:
Issue summary
- Northstar Search reports higher p95 latency on a single Dedicated chat route after enabling a Quantization Profile Library profile.
- Regression is most visible on decode latency (streaming token cadence slower); p50 mostly unchanged.

Customer impact
- Customer reports p95 latency increased from ~1.3s to ~2.1s end-to-end on their main chat route.
- They are running near their throughput target; tail latency is causing user-visible delays.

Environment
- Dedicated cluster: nsr-dedicated-prod-01
- Region: us-east
- Route: chat-prod (route_id: rte_9b1d3a)
- Model: rw-llama3-70b-instruct
- Quantization setting change: quantization_profile_ref set from "default" to "qpl://rw-llama3-70b-instruct/int8w-fp16a/v1.2.0" at 2025-02-22 18:42 UTC

Steps to reproduce (internal)
1) Send streaming chat requests (typical prompt length 6–10k tokens; max_new_tokens 300–700) to rte_9b1d3a.
2) Compare baseline (quantization_profile_ref=default) vs enabled profile.
3) Observe p95 decode time and p95 time-to-first-token (TTFT).

Initial triage observations
- Onset aligns with route-level enablement of the INT8 profile.
- No concurrent deploys on the dedicated cluster besides the config change.
- Error rate unchanged (no 5xx spike), but queueing time increased under load.

Dashboards / logs (internal)
- Dedicated route overview (latency): https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/dedicated-route/dedicated-route-latency?var=cluster=nsr-dedicated-prod-01&var=route=rte_9b1d3a
- Runtime breakdown (TTFT/decode): https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/runtime-latency/runtime-latency-breakdown?var=model=rw-llama3-70b-instruct&var=cluster=nsr-dedicated-prod-01
- Quant profile panels (applied/fallback rates): https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/quant-profiles/quant-profile-rollout?var=route=rte_9b1d3a
- Trace search (quant_profile_id tag): https://traces.redwood.ai/search?service=runtime&tag.route_id=rte_9b1d3a

Investigation notes
- Quant profile was applied (not fallback) for the majority of requests; however we saw an elevated "profile_apply_slow_path" counter correlated with long-context prompts.
- KV cache metrics show higher VRAM pressure and increased "kv_cache_evictions" after enabling the profile, likely due to changed memory layout + smaller headroom for long-context sequences.
- Under the customer’s traffic mix (long prompts), the INT8 profile shifts us into a kernel path that is optimal for throughput at moderate contexts but increases tail latency at ~8k–12k context due to additional staging / dequant overhead and more frequent cache pressure.
- Batching remained enabled; p95 queue time increased because decode took longer, reducing effective throughput.

Mitigation taken
- Rolled back route-level setting to "default" precision (baseline) at 2025-02-22 22:17 UTC.
- Confirmed p95 recovered within ~15 minutes (after in-flight requests drained and cache stabilized).

Resolution
- Root cause: profile qpl://rw-llama3-70b-instruct/int8w-fp16a/v1.2.0 is not suitable for Northstar’s long-context workload on their dedicated GPU SKU; it increases VRAM pressure and triggers a slower decode path at high context lengths, worsening p95.
- Customer kept feature enabled on a lower-traffic staging route for continued evaluation, but production route is baseline.

Next steps / follow-ups
- Applied ML to publish an updated profile variant with a stricter max_context constraint and/or alternate kernel preference for this GPU class.
- Runtime team to add a guardrail/compat warning for this profile when typical_context_len > 8k on the relevant SKU class (doc + console warning).
- CS to provide customer with an eval plan: run A/B at 1–5% traffic with long-context prompt set and monitor kv_cache_evictions + decode p95 before re-enabling.

Customer-facing summary (for email)
- We confirmed the latency regression was caused by the newly enabled quantization profile on your production route. We rolled back the profile on that route and latency returned to baseline. The profile is performing worse for your long-context workload on the current hardware; we’re working on a revised profile/compat constraints before recommending re-enable.

Determined the enabled INT8 profile increased tail latency for the customer’s long-context workload due to VRAM pressure and slow-path decode behavior; awaiting updated profile/constraints before re-enablement.
